title: Interviews still needed in SIU probe
article: Witnesses remain to be interviewed by the province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) nearly a month after an Ottawa-area man was killed in a confrontation with police north of Brockville.
Officials at the SIU said some interviews were still outstanding as of Thursday afternoon.

SIU spokesman Jasbir Brar was not sure whether the two subject officers in the incident had spoken to the agency yet, but added the SIU should have an update on the status of the investigation next week.
"The investigation is actively ongoing," she said, adding it was hard to tell how long it might last.
"Every case is different."
Meanwhile, the regional coroner said he is waiting for the SIU probe to wrap up before deciding whether to hold an inquest into the death of Phillip Jeffrey Charbonneau.
The 35-year-old resident of Hammond, in Prescott-Russell, died in a confrontation with police at Forthton on the night of July 3.
Ontario Provincial Police officers shot and killed Charbonneau after he allegedly struck an officer with his pickup truck.

The OPP says two police officers suffered minor injuries in the incident, which resulted from a chase after Charbonneau allegedly bolted from a Reduce Impaired Driving Everywhere (RIDE) check on the Highway 401 off-ramp at County Road 29 in Brockville around 11 p.m. on that Friday.

According to the SIU, a civilian agency that investigates incidents involving serious injuries or deaths involving police, the OPP's attempt to block the fleeing suspect "resulted in a collision between the truck and OPP vehicles."
Officers then "interacted" with the suspect and "at some point the truck struck an officer," the agency has said.
"Two officers discharged their firearms and the driver was struck at least once.
The male was pronounced dead at the scene," the SIU statement adds.
The SIU currently has two "subject officers" in the investigation and eight "witness officers."
Under the law, witness officers are required to co-operate with the SIU, while subject officers have the right not to speak to investigators.
Dr. Roger Skinner, the regional supervising coroner for eastern Ontario, said Thursday he is letting the SIU do its work first.
"There won't be any determination made until they complete their investigation."
Certain circumstances would prompt a mandatory investigation, noted Skinner.
Such would be the case if it's determined Charbonneau died while in custody.
In other cases, noted Skinner, the call for an inquest is at the coroner's discretion.
The SIU's findings would be part of either decision.

Julie Young, who lives in an apartment above the Cedar Valley Golf and Country Club near the scene of the incident and saw some of it unfold, said she was interviewed by SIU investigators earlier this month at her workplace.
She has given them pictures she took from her apartment window and an SIU photographer later came to her apartment to verify the angle from which her photos were shot, she said.
OPP officers conducting an internal investigation also came to her apartment to interview her about the incident, said Young.
"It was done very professionally," said Young. "Everybody was totally above board."
SIU officials said they were being careful because any evidence they gather could be used in a coroner's inquest, said Young.
